findings.summary: the refusal path calls clear_resume_launching, which takes the pointer lock blocking, so against a real promotion holding both locks the resume waits instead of refusing
promotion_lock_name restates the lock name owned by promotion.py:162, so a rename there silently disables the guard with no test reddening
resume_plan mutates the pointer before mark_resume_launching, so the guard fires after the write it exists to prevent
DECLARED_MUTATION is defined and never referenced
the log's module header names the worktree module while its tree and cwd headers name the scratch tree, so the header misreports which code ran

raw_text:
VERDICT goal: the node goal is "a resume refuses while its run's promotion lock is held"; reckon/crew/resumption.py:236-256 takes the run's promotion lock non-blocking inside mark_resume_launching and raises a CrewError naming the promotion, so the stated deliverable is present.
VERDICT done_when: the done_when asks for a refusal that leaves the pointer unchanged, a resume without a promotion proceeding, a five-second deadlock bound, importer arms adding no failure and ruff clean; tests/test_a_resume_waits_out_a_promotion.py:110-223 supplies each case and the manifest records head 3 passed against base 1 failed/2 passed with identical importer failure ids.
VERDICT write_paths: the declared paths are reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/crew/resumption.py, tests/test_a_resume_waits_out_a_promotion.py and the evidence fragment; git diff --stat from the base to the head touches exactly those four files and nothing else.
VERDICT manifest: read at its own path; it states status complete, carries all six rubric lines, records head 3 passed and base 1 failed/2 passed with both logs under the run directory, and names eleven pre-existing importer failures under outside_scope.
VERDICT diff: read commit by commit; the first commit adds PointerLockHeldError and the blocking flag to reckon/crew/runs.py:452-490 and the promotion-lock take to reckon/crew/resumption.py:236-256, and the second adds the test and the evidence fragment, all inside the declared scope.
CALL_SITES: reckon/crew/resumption.py:_resume (line 1771), reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:resume_plan (line 1440), reckon/crew/promotion.py:_promotion_lock (line 162)
SCORE goal_fidelity: 17
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/resumption.py:236-256 refuses with a message naming the promotion, though the refusal is reached only after clear_resume_launching takes the pointer lock blocking at resumption.py:262.
SCORE evidence: 16
JUSTIFICATION evidence: head-suite.log records 3 passed at the reviewed head and negative-control-base-arm.log records 1 failed/2 passed with EXIT=1 at the base, but the refusal case at tests/test_a_resume_waits_out_a_promotion.py:139 holds only the promotion lock, not the run's pointer lock that promotion.py:2072 also holds.
SCORE scope_discipline: 20
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: git diff --stat from the base to the head shows four files, every one of them inside the manifest's declared write paths.
SCORE durability: 15
JUSTIFICATION durability: tests/test_a_resume_waits_out_a_promotion.py:110 fails at the base revision with DID NOT RAISE CrewError, but no assertion reddens if promotion.py:162 renames its lock, because resumption.py:212 restates the name independently.
SCORE fit: 18
JUSTIFICATION fit: PointerLockHeldError and the blocking keyword on _pointer_lock follow the existing contextmanager idiom at reckon/crew/runs.py:465 and carry no plan or ticket identifier, though the test's unused DECLARED_MUTATION at tests/test_a_resume_waits_out_a_promotion.py:40 is dead weight.
SCORE reuse: 5
JUSTIFICATION reuse: reckon/crew/resumption.py:212 restates the lock name that reckon/crew/promotion.py:162 already owns instead of extending that owner with a blocking parameter.
FINDING reckon/crew/resumption.py:262 non-blocking: the refusal path reaches clear_resume_launching from the exception arm at resumption.py:1808, and that helper takes the run's pointer lock with a blocking _pointer_lock, so against a real promotion, which holds both locks at promotion.py:2072, the resume waits for the promotion to end before raising, contrary to the message's refusal-rather-than-waiting claim and to the fragment's; the new test cannot see this because it holds only the promotion lock.
FINDING reckon/crew/resumption.py:212 non-blocking: promotion_lock_name restates the promotion lock name owned by reckon/crew/promotion.py:162 and repeated at promotion.py:199, so a rename there silently makes the resume take a different lock and the guard vanishes, with no test reddening because the refusal test spells the literal itself and the deadlock test would simply stop contending.
FINDING reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1435 non-blocking: resume_plan mutates the pointer through _mutate_pointer before calling mark_resume_launching at line 1440, so on that path the new guard fires after the pointer write it exists to prevent, and the manifest's evidence_inputs overstates the call site by saying it is refused with the same message.
FINDING tests/test_a_resume_waits_out_a_promotion.py:40 non-blocking: DECLARED_MUTATION is defined and never referenced, leaving a dead constant that reads as a check but asserts nothing.
FINDING /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261109T215635060576-a-resume-refuses-while-its-run-is-promoted/negative-control-base-arm.log:3 non-blocking: the header's module line names the worktree's reckon/crew/resumption.py while its tree and cwd lines name the scratch tree, and the manifest's measurement_module names the scratch path, so the log's record of which module ran contradicts its other header lines.
